intro: This question helps us find the best place for you to begin.

widget.instructions: The grid shows a and b. Turn on Show components to see each vector split into its î and ĵ parts.

stem: Find the scalar product a · b.

hints.text: The scalar product pairs up matching components. Which component of a goes with which component of b?
Multiply x with x and y with y, then add: a·b = a₁b₁ + a₂b₂.

cross-multiplied-components.text: You multiplied x with y. The scalar product pairs î with î and ĵ with ĵ, because î·ĵ = 0.

ignored-angle.text: |a||b| is the scalar product only when the vectors point the same way. In general it is |a||b| cos θ, which the components give directly. The highlighted projection shows how much of a lies along b.

dropped-j-term.text: That's only the î part. Add the ĵ part too.

generic.text: Pair matching components, multiply each pair, then add.

workedSolution.text: a·b = a₁b₁ + a₂b₂, because î·î = ĵ·ĵ = 1 and î·ĵ = 0.
= {{dot}}. Geometrically, that is |b| times the projection of a onto b.

cross-multiplied-components.front: a = a₁î + a₂ĵ, b = b₁î + b₂ĵ. What is a·b?

ignored-angle.back: No: a·b = |a||b| cos θ. It equals |a||b| only when θ = 0.

dropped-j-term.front: How many terms does a·b have for 2-D vectors?
